title: Direct OpenCode HTTP Scope Decision
claim: FP-MCP-291 chooses the lower-risk Option B: direct OpenCode HTTP is permanently narrower-scoped as a design, canary, endpoint-shape, assistant-completion, and planning tool, and must not carry implementation execution authority for real workspace-changing code edits; real workspace-changing work remains assigned to the guarded/worker path and its safety gates.
summary: FP-MCP-291 resolves the fork left open by FP-MCP-289 and FP-MCP-290. The decision rejects maintaining two independent proven-safe execution paths indefinitely. Direct HTTP remains useful for bounded planning and canary interactions, but it is not safety-equivalent to FP-027 and must not be used to satisfy FP-027 by resemblance. The abort question for direct HTTP is closed by scope rather than by equivalence: session deletion remains not admitted as a proven abort primitive, but no direct-HTTP abort primitive is required while direct HTTP remains outside real workspace-changing work. Any future attempt to expand direct HTTP beyond this scope is an architecture reversal requiring a new auditor-reviewed packet and missing safety-property proofs before scope changes. Steering docs were updated in commit dc6b6d3. No implementation, execution, approval consumption, disable switch change, OpenCode start, runner-start contact, or server.ts refactor is authorized by this packet.
caveats: This decision does not prove or implement direct-HTTP abort semantics.
This decision does not weaken FP-027; FP-027 remains open and unsatisfied.
This decision forecloses incremental direct-HTTP capability creep: expansion requires a new architecture-reversal packet.
Direct HTTP can still be used for bounded design/canary/planning interactions that do not perform real workspace-changing work.
The server.ts refactor must use the accepted guarded/worker path or human/GPT manual maintenance under explicit packet boundaries, not direct-HTTP execution authority.
boundaries: no implementation changes beyond steering documentation

decisionRationale: avoids maintaining two parallel proven-safe run paths
preserves guarded/worker path as the code-edit execution authority path
keeps direct HTTP useful without expanding its risk surface
directHttpAllowedUses: planning interactions without real workspace-changing work
directHttpForbiddenUses: quiet capability accumulation without architecture reversal

abortPrimitiveDecision.reason: closed by narrowed scope, not by equivalence
abortPrimitiveDecision.futureExpansionRequirement: any future direct-HTTP execution-authority proposal must prove or build abort-equivalent semantics before scope expansion
